No. The custodian's 2025 loss of **$46,708.51** on the joint account's Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund sale stands as reported. No purchase in the files falls inside the 30-day wash-sale window, so none of the loss is disallowed.

**The loss.** There was one sale at a loss in a taxable account in 2025. The joint account (SYN-95710001) sold 812 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund on 2025-11-03. The custodian reports proceeds of $215,277.44 against a cost basis of $261,985.95, a long-term covered loss of $46,708.51. The 1099-B shows the same figures, with no wash-sale adjustment. The two IRAs are not taxable accounts, so they report no realized gains or losses.

**Purchases near the sale.** The wash-sale window is 30 days either side of the 2025-11-03 trade date, so 2025-10-04 through 2025-12-03.
- **Before the sale:** no Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund was bought in any account between 2025-10-04 and 2025-11-03.
- **Elena's IRA, 500 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund on 2025-12-04:** buying in an IRA can trigger a wash sale. But 2025-12-04 is 31 days after the sale, one day past the window, which ends 2025-12-03. The trade date is what counts, and settlement (2025-12-05) is later still. So this purchase doesn't disallow anything. It came very close, though, and anyone checking it should know that.
- **Joint account, 4,200 Ridgeholm Equal Weight Fund on 2025-11-03:** this buy happened the same day, so it is inside the window. But Ridgeholm Equal Weight Fund is a different security from Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund (SEC-0027 vs SEC-0025). One caveat: the files don't say which index each fund tracks. If they track their usual real-world indexes, Ridgeholm Equal Weight Fund (equal-weight S&P 500) and Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund (S&P MidCap 400) are not substantially identical. I've treated it that way.
- **Graham's IRA:** it made no Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund purchases.

There are no carryforwards from 2024 (zero short- and long-term in the tax profile). The full $46,708.51 is allowed for 2025, before the $3,000 annual limit on capital losses against ordinary income.
